decisions.reason: Retaining AXP2101 specifies the separate integrated-board power-management Requirement but does not change the single-board consolidation or functionality-preservation attributes.
Keeping AXP2101 does not revoke the cheapest-practical-design goal or the qualified preference to use JLCPCB Basic components wherever possible.
This Requirement governs source OR-ing in the existing multi-board main-board design; selecting AXP2101 for the new integrated board does not change that topology.
The source confirms the integrated board's PMIC selection but does not change the existing power board's DCDC1 setpoint or compensation rule.
The PMIC selection for the integrated design does not alter the connector inventory or connector architecture of the existing main board.
Retaining AXP2101 has no necessary effect on the LED board's 3.3V and data pin ordering.
Although both Requirements involve AXP2101, the source selects the component for the integrated board and does not modify the existing power board's VMID/VSYS or thermal-pad topology.
The integrated-board PMIC choice does not change the existing main board's INA3221 rail-monitoring coverage or placement.
The source does not change the existing power board's battery connector, voltage range, pinout, placement, or connection destination.
Selecting AXP2101 for integrated power management does not itself revise the existing power board's battery-protection modes or cutoff values.
The integrated-board power-management component decision does not alter the existing main board's panel controls, GPIO mappings, or power-button connector.
Retaining AXP2101 does not necessarily change the existing main board's 3.3V LED supply, direct data drive, or level-shifter decision.
